2.full_quote: You did amazing. You did amazing because before we would stop around with three left. So little by little your mechanism is going to go in place — the shape of your instrument was straight up and down, you had more height. So just keep — when you watch back the video and you practice with your video, make sure that you're straight up and down.
2.why_it_hooks: Real-time proof of progress plus a self-check the student can do alone with her own video, not just in the lesson.
2.suggested_caption: Watch your own video back. Are you straight up and down?

3.full_quote: Anyway, at the back of the book, there are five tasks in the pearl section. And task number three is what you're going to have to do for each of the songs. So for last month's song and for the three songs that you do this month, you're going to write down all the lyrics with spaces in between. And on our next lesson, we will go through the breath marks, the diction, and the emotional tenor.
3.why_it_hooks: Shows the actual structured method behind the coaching — most students never see a curriculum this deliberate for something as intuitive-seeming as singing a song.
3.suggested_caption: Every song gets broken down into breath marks, diction, and emotion. On purpose.

4.full_quote: Better. I also think that at the closer to the end of the class I started to feel my voice better, because in the beginning I was a little bit shaky. Probably with practice it will be gone, but now at least I feel a little bit more this switch. I will work on the clarity, but at least now I see that, okay, here I'm ground control, here I'm ground control, here I'm major tom, and so on and so forth. But I love this song because it's so different, like you can really play these characters, and I mean it's a challenge but I like it.
4.why_it_hooks: An unprompted, in-her-own-words moment of a student feeling her own progress mid-lesson — real social proof, not a coach's claim.
4.suggested_caption: "By the end of class, I started to feel my voice better."
